ashura-march.title: Ashura march, Tehran, 11 December 1978
ashura-march.note: Route and timings are approximate. Marchers came from all over the city; this shows the main column along Shahreza and Eisenhower Avenues.

markers.label: Shahyad Square: the resolution is read

captions.text: Morning of Ashura. Crowds gather in the east and south of the city and set off west along Shahreza Avenue.
Marshals from the mosques keep order. Women march in their own sections, many in black chadors.
Past the University of Tehran. The government has agreed to keep troops away from the route.
The column fills Eisenhower Avenue for kilometres. Estimates for Tehran run from a few hundred thousand to two million.
At Shahyad Square a seventeen-point resolution is read: Khomeini is leader, and the monarchy must end.
The crowds disperse peacefully. Five weeks later the Shah leaves Iran.

khomeini-return.title: Khomeini's return, 1 February 1979
khomeini-return.note: Route and timings are approximate. The crowds slowed the motorcade so much that Khomeini made the last part of the journey by helicopter.

markers.label: Behesht-e Zahra: 'I will appoint a government'

captions.text: 9:30 in the morning. Khomeini's chartered Air France jet lands at Mehrabad after fifteen years of exile.
He speaks briefly at the airport, then sets off into the city. Millions of people line the streets.
The car crawls along Eisenhower Avenue. People climb onto it and the crowd closes round it.
The motorcade can barely move. A helicopter lifts Khomeini the rest of the way to the cemetery.
At Behesht-e Zahra, among the graves of the year's dead, he calls Bakhtiar's government illegal and says he will appoint his own.
